A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HelpSteer2-Preference work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains Appendices A-I and adds Appendices J-M.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation analyses, reward-model experiments and alignment experiments, including results in Section 2 and Tables 1 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds reward-model ablations, alignment controls and capability evaluations in Tables 11-13.

M1.justification: The regression and Bradley-Terry objectives, regression-initialized Scaled BT with ExPO, and DPO/PPO/REINFORCE procedures remain unchanged. Appendix K tests alternative preprocessing and training order as ablation controls; the proposed pipeline is retained.

E1.justification: Appendix M adds MMLU, GSM8K and HumanEval evaluations for REINFORCE and its starting model. This substantially extends aligned-model coverage from the existing instruction-following benchmarks to targeted knowledge, mathematics and coding capability retention. Training-data coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The main comparison sets remain unchanged. Appendix L newly evaluates Llama3-70B-SteerLM-RM as an alternative reward model for PPO; previously it appeared only as a RewardBench comparator. Appendix K also adds a reversed-order BT-to-regression training comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments vary annotation filtering and aggregation, remove prompts flagged by shared 7-grams, and replace collected preferences with converted ratings. Appendix M adds five-shot MMLU and zero-shot GSM8K/HumanEval protocols, all without chain-of-thought. These substantially expand the evaluation design while retaining the original experiments' settings.

E4.justification: Appendices K-L add controls examining filtering, prompt overlap, rating conversion, training order and reward-model choice. Appendix M tests capability retention after REINFORCE, while Appendix J illustrates loss behavior across representative cases. These materially extend v1's existing justifier ablations, Chat-Hard analysis and reward curves.

E5.justification: Both versions report AlpacaEval standard errors and Arena Hard confidence intervals. Table 12 extends that existing practice to new comparisons. No new seed information, repeated-training-run counts or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Existing results, including 94.1 on RewardBench and 85.0 on Arena Hard, are unchanged. Tables 10-13 add loss calculations, ablation outcomes and capability scores: the overlap-removal control scores 93.3 versus the 93.7 reference, while REINFORCE/starting-model scores are 82.4/82.2 on MMLU, 90.9/91.6 on GSM8K and 83.5/80.5 on HumanEval. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical loss definitions remain unchanged. Appendix J introduces illustrative substitutions into those formulas and informal mechanism arguments; its reward-gap notation restates the existing setup. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The dataset and complementary reward-model contributions remain intact. The abstract strengthens the alignment claim by explicitly identifying REINFORCE's 85.0 Arena Hard score as number one as of 1 October 2024. The score itself was already reported in v1's Table 4.

C2.justification: Appendices J-M add explanations concerning annotation-noise resistance, filtering benefits, complementary labels and unsuccessful reverse initialization. They acknowledge 42 potentially overlapping prompts and interpret the removal experiment as showing limited impact. They also interpret the new capability results as evidence against catastrophic forgetting; the noise-resistance mechanism remains a hypothesis.

D1.justification: v2 adds an instruct-model access link, the shared-7-gram overlap criterion, and learning-rate/KL settings for the added controls. Existing preprocessing instructions, training hyperparameters and hardware/compute disclosures in Appendices C, E and F remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Appendix A remain the same. HelpSteer and HelpSteer2 references receive publication-metadata updates, which do not constitute additions to the related literature.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and contribution wording, fixes several language issues, updates the publication header and adds appendix cross-references. It removes the standalone conclusion and appends Sections J-M, but largely preserves the existing prose and narrative organization.

P2.justification: New Tables 10-13 substantially expand the displays to cover loss behavior, reward-model ablations, alignment ablations and capability retention. Existing Tables 1-9 and Figures 1-3 are retained. Figure 3 is repositioned, and the front-page resource links are reformatted.

improvement.justification: Appendices K-L address important validation gaps in v1's central claims through controls for converted ratings, filtering and training order, plus retraining after removing potentially overlapping prompts. Appendix M adds capability-retention evidence where v1 deferred broader evaluation. These additions substantially strengthen empirical support and transparency, although small score differences still lack training-run uncertainty and Appendix J's noise-resistance explanation remains speculative.
